title: SRE ops deck outline + playbook notes (prep)
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratch for the SRE weekly ops sync (reliability review). Use this to shape the 10–12 slide deck and playbook updates; keep it scannable for oncall and TLs.

Meeting goals (30m):
- Confirm SLO status + risk (2 min)
- Review paging trends and root causes (8–10 min)
- Top incidents and action-item followups (10 min)
- Decisions / triage for constrained capacity and planned mitigations (5–8 min)

High-level headline (what I want to convey):
- SLOs: still within soft error budget but trending worse on tail latency spikes; main culprit: model OOMs on bursty long-context requests after new quantized model rollout.
- Paging: volume up 35% week-over-week; majority are high-cpu spool and OOM alerts (pager noise from a single customer job pattern).
- Incidents: 2 P1s in last 2 weeks (OOM cascade 2026-08-15, Region failover flapping 2026-08-09) — both have follow-ups but we need concrete owners and deadlines.

SLO snapshot (to include a slide):
- Target: latency P95 < 300ms (inference-hosted-prod) and availability 99.95% (token-generation API).
- Current (rolling 30d): availability 99.86% -> error budget burn ~0.09 (9% of budget spent in last 30d? note: reconcile metric source; dash shows 0.09 absolute).
- Key drift: tail latency P99 up from 420ms -> 680ms over last 7d.
- Hypothesis: memory pressure + increased request max_seq length after model rollout -> more KV cache thrashing and occasional OOMs -> fallbacks + retries -> increased latencies and accounted errors.

Pager trend notes (for slide and quick talking points):
- Total pages: +35% WoW. Top categories: OOM (45%), high CPU loop (30%), network error bursts (15%), others (10%).
- Paging heatmap: spike at 2026-08-15 03:20 UTC (OOM cascade across three pods).
- Caller pattern: single large customer training/inference job misconfigured to use hosted inference API w/ huge context — needs CS outreach. Ticket: INF-2345.
- Noise reduction idea: add short-term suppression for repeated identical OOM pages within 10 minutes for the same customer-id + correlate with 'job-id' (low-risk).

Top incidents (short recaps):
1) 2026-08-15 OOM cascade (P1)
   - Summary: new quantized variant (v2-q4) rolled to cluster group A; under long-context bursts, KV allocation triggered OOM and node autoscale thrash; fallback caused retry storms on adjacent region -> elevated latencies and >30 min availability impact for some customers.
   - Root cause: quantized model memory estimation mismatch + lack of per-customer sequence length caps on hosted tier.
   - Current state: postmortem draft in Confluence (link above). Mitigation implemented: rollback of v2-q4 in cluster group A + emergency config that limits max_seq to 4096 for affected clusters.
   - Action items: 
     * PR for improved memory modeling for quantized kernels (owner: Marco, GH PR linked) — due 2026-08-27.
     * Add sequence-length quota enforcement at API layer (owner: Jesse) — target 2026-09-03 (needs product alignment).
     * Postmortem review with CS/customer (owner: Ravi) — 2026-08-24.

2) 2026-08-09 Region failover flapping (P2->P1 initially)
   - Summary: transient flapping between AZs triggered by overloaded storage controller used by cache layer; degraded routing and elevated 5xx.
   - Mitigation: storage controller patch applied; routing fallback improved.
   - Remaining: add synthetic checks to detect storage-backend latency and trigger early fallback.
   - Owner: SRE infra (Anika) — task SRE-112, due 2026-08-28.

Playbook / runbook updates (bullet list to put in the repo):
- OOM cascade response checklist (new):
  1) Identify model variant + cluster group -> command list to isolate (kubectl + metric queries).
  2) Temporarily scale out with extra mem-heavy nodes + disable autoscale thrashing toggles.
  3) Roll back variant to previous stable.
  4) Add customer seq-length cap and throttle at API gateway for offending job.
  5) Postmortem template: include model memory profile snapshot and kernel logs.
- Oncall diagnostic shortcuts to add to pb (short cmds): kv-cache-status.sh, infer-oom-tail.sh, request-replay-lite.py (link to /tools).

Open questions to raise in sync (note form):
- Do we want system-level automatic sequence-length clamp on hosted tier until model memory estimation is fixed? Pros: immediate safety. Cons: possible customer impact & product approval needed. (quick vote)
- Acceptable suppression window for repeated identical OOM pages? 5m vs 10m? Tradeoffs: detection vs silence.
- How aggressive do we want rollout gating for quantized variants (canary size)? Proposal: require 2-day canary + synthetic long-context test pass before wider rollout.

Decision proposals (prep to ask for):
- Approve temporary system clamp: max_seq=4096 for hosted-prod for next 2 weeks (owner: product + infra) — vote during sync.
- Adopt 10-minute dedupe window for identical OOM pages from same job-id (owner: SRE tooling).
- Require synthetic long-context test as a hard gating check in the model release checklist for quantized variants.

Action items (capture for follow-up):
- Jesse: implement API-level seq-length clamp and add toggle flag (due 2026-09-03).
- Marco: PR memory-estimation model for quantized kernels + benchmark (draft by 2026-08-27).
- Ravi: customer outreach & alignment on seq clamp (meeting w/ CS + customer 8/24).
- Anika: add synthetic storage-backend check to routing (task SRE-112) — due 8/28.
- Me (Evelyn): draft slide deck + short TL notes, circulate by 2026-08-21 morning; pull metric queries and paste into slide appendix.

Deck outline (slide by slide quick):
1) Title / TL;DR (2 bullets)
2) SLO snapshot (1 chart + heatmap)
3) Pager trend summary (bar chart categories)
4) Top incidents (2 slides: one each)
5) Playbook updates & quick commands
6) Proposed decisions & vote
7) Action items & owners
8) Appendix: detailed queries and ticket links

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep slides minimal; point people to postmortem for details.
- Bring one concrete ask to unblock: approve clamp OR approve additional canary gating.
- Call out customer-impacted IDs (redact PII) and ensure CS is looped before wider communication.

Small checklist before sync (today):
- [x] Pull latest SLO metrics (dashboard snapshot).
- [x] Verify postmortem draft link is accessible to meeting attendees.
- [ ] Draft 3 slides + TL;DR (due EOD 2026-08-21).
- [ ] Ping product for fast approval on temporary clamp (slack: @product-tl).
- [ ] Confirm Jesse has capacity to start API clamp work this sprint.

Slack blurbs to send after meeting (templates):
- To oncall channel: "SRE sync note: OOM cascade 8/15 — rollback done; temporary seq clamp proposed. Postmortem link: <link>. Action owners: Jesse, Marco, Ravi, Anika."
- To CS: "Heads-up: proposing temporary seq-length clamp for hosted-prod while we stabilize quantized model memory estimates. We'll coordinate outreach for affected customers.",
